thread:
support-liz: FYI customer acme is seeing a big p95/p99 jump on /v1/generate since 2026-03-15T09:10Z. They reported tail latency ~800-1200ms. Traces show tons of cache-miss tags and eviction spikes.
sre-jen: Can you paste the quick trace/log sample and any recent deploys?
support-liz: Logs attached below (redacted ids). We also have a support ticket with repro curl.
support-liz: ```
[2026-03-15T09:11:45Z] route=generate req=rx8 model=redwood-xl-1 prefix_key="user:123:welcome" cache_hit=false eviction=true eviction_reason="ttl" kv_hash=0x3fa1
[2026-03-15T09:11:46Z] route=generate req=ry2 model=redwood-xl-1 prefix_key="User:123:Welcome" cache_hit=false eviction=true eviction_reason="ttl" kv_hash=0x4b2c
[2026-03-15T09:11:47Z] route=generate req=rz5 model=redwood-xl-1 prefix_key="user:123:welcome
" cache_hit=false eviction=true eviction_reason="ttl" kv_hash=0x1a9f
metrics: kv_evictions_per_sec: 48 -> 970, kv_miss_rate_p95: 0.12 -> 0.87, p95_latency: 120ms -> 860ms
```
sre-jen: Who pushed the recent runtime change? I see a deploy-bot webhook around 09:08.
deploy-bot: deploy started: service=runtime commit=4c2b9e env=prod by=dev-ops-ron at=2026-03-15T09:07:59Z
aj: Looking at logs — prefix_key variants with different casing/whitespace. Sounds like key normalization was disabled. Any config toggle?
dev-ops-ron: I rolled a small perf toggle in that deploy to disable prefix normalizer to cut CPU for hot-path hashing. PR 1234. Reason was micro-optimization for a high-throughput customer.
maria: That would fragment the hotset. If normalization off, semantically identical prefixes produce different keys -> massive cardinality increase.
tim: Can we flip feature-flag back? If that's the cause a rollback or re-enable should restore hit rates quickly.
support-liz: Repro curl from customer (anonymized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-1","input":"Hello"}'
```
They claim their client sometimes sends slightly different whitespace/casing in prefix metadata header which used to be normalized server-side.
aj: Quick triage idea: enable normalization feature flag for the impacted shard pool, and trigger a small background prefill job to warm top prefixes. That should reduce p95 within a few minutes.
sre-jen: Agreed. Ron can you toggle for prod? Also we should throttle renegade eviction TTL and temporarily switch eviction policy from pure TTL to LRU for affected pools to avoid evicting hot keys fast.
dev-ops-ron: I can flip normalization flag on shard pool a,b,c now. Doing it.
dev-ops-ron: toggled prefix_normalization=on for shardpool-a,b at 09:23:12Z — monitoring.
maria: Start a prefill job for observed top-100 prefixes (based on last hour). I can run a one-off job to re-populate KV.
sre-jen: Also bump the in-memory max_entries for those pools by +20% to buy time while warmup runs.
tim: For a more robust mitigation, add a canonicalization step at ingress that normalizes casing/trim, and add unit tests simulating client variations.
aj: Important: add a realtime metric for "prefix_cardinality" and the 99th percentile cardinality delta so we detect this automatically.
support-liz: Customer confirmed tail improved from 1.1s -> 160ms after normalization toggled and prefill started (partial improvement). They're still seeing occasional spikes during redeploys.
aj: Redeploys likely clear in-memory cache. We need persistent warmup at rollout and a graceful drain strategy (drain traffic off nodes then warmup before cutting).
maria: Action items: 1) PR to re-enable normalization by default + tests (maria/aj) 2) Add rollout warmup job to infra (maria) 3) Add metric/dashboard alert for prefix_cardinality and eviction spike (aj) 4) Short-term: durable prefill + increase max_entries (dev-ops-ron) 5) Postmortem + customer communication (sre-jen/support-liz).
sre-jen: I'll open an incident ticket and assign owners. Also recommend a small perf regression test to ensure normalization cost is acceptable.
support-liz: Customer CS updated and happy with interim fix. We'll schedule a follow-up for formal RC and postmortem. :thumbsup:
aj: One more note — add normalization idempotency in logs so we can confirm keys are canonical in traces (e.g., canonical_prefix="user:123:welcome").
maria: I'll start on the PR after lunch.
dev-ops-ron: Filed rollback-safe deploy checklist item to ensure warmup runs pre-cutover.
sre-jen: Thanks team — leaving monitoring on this for next 24h. Keep thread updated with any anomalies.
